Both compiled and correct (5/5), running at 45.7ms vs 56.8ms reference — my AveLang kernel is actually 1.24x faster than the reference in this configuration.

The implementation has three key components:

**`gemm_scale_bias_kernel`** — A tiled GEMM kernel with 64×64 output tiles and 16-element K tiles, using 256 threads per block (1D). It loads BF16 A and B matrices into shared memory, accumulates in FP32, and fuses the Linear bias addition and element-wise scale multiplication into the write-back. The shared memory tiles (64×16 BF16 each for A and B) fit within 4KB total.

**`batchnorm_eval_kernel`** — An eval-mode batchnorm kernel that applies `(x - running_mean) / sqrt(running_var + eps) * gamma + beta` per channel. Launches one block per output channel (4096 blocks), with each 256-thread block processing its column in strided fashion.

**Host wrapper** — `ModelNew.forward` extracts weights from the PyTorch layers, converts them to FP32 for the bias/scale/norm parameters (for numerical stability), converts inputs to BF16 for the GEMM, launches both kernels, and converts the final output to BF16 to match the reference dtype.

The kernel passes all 5 correctness trials and completes in ~46ms with CUDA graph capture on an AMD MI300X (gfx942).
